title: a declaration inside an expression block follows ordinary lexical scope: it is visible to the block's value break and does not leak into or collide with the enclosing scope
notes: specification/control-flow.mdx, 'Blocks': 'An expression block MAY produce a value from its final expression or from a labeled value break. **A declaration inside an expression block follows ordinary lexical scope.**' The second sentence had no case. It is load-bearing for the lowering rather than decorative: poc/src/language/README.md records that a labeled block value is recovered by rewriting `break :label value` into `{ value; break label; }` and placing the labeled statement BEFORE a marker-initialized host declaration — a textual move that hoists the block out of the expression it was written in. A move that also hoisted the block's own `const` would put `candidate` in the enclosing function scope, where the later `const candidate = "outer"` is a redeclaration; the same name is reused here on purpose so that leak is an error rather than a silent shadow, and the two distinct printed values show the inner binding was the one the break read.
